'''''Glyceria''''' is a widespread genus of [[Poaceae|grass family]] common across [[Eurasia]], Australia, [[North Africa]], and the [[Americas]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/2954335#page/47/mode/1up Brown, Robert, 1810.  Prodromus Florae Novae Hollandiae 179] in Latin</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=113749 Flora of China Vol. 22 Page 213 <big>甜茅属</big> tian mao shu ''Glyceria'' R. Brown, Prodr. 179. 1810. ]</ref><ref>[https://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Glyceria Altervista Flora Italiana genere ''Glyceria'']</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:575457 |title=Atlas of Living Australia, ''Glyceria'' R.Br., Sweetgrass |access-date=2015-03-27 |archive-date=2016-05-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160513234530/http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:575457 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

''Glyceria'' is known commonly as '''mannagrass''' in the United States, or, in the UK, '''sweet-grass'''. These are perennial [[Rhizome|rhizomatous]] grasses found in wet areas in temperate regions worldwide. The base of the grass grows along the ground and may root at several places. Then it grows erect and bears leaf blades which may be flat or folded. The [[panicle]] inflorescences nod when heavy.  Some mannagrasses are considered weeds while others are endangered in their native habitats.<ref>[https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?8738,9033 Jepson Manual Treatment]</ref><ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=GLYCE United States Department of Agriculture Plants Profile]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://herbarium.usu.edu/webmanual/info2.asp?name=Glyceria&type=treatment |title=Grass Manual Account |access-date=2007-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611123115/http://herbarium.usu.edu/webmanual/info2.asp?name=Glyceria&type=treatment |archive-date=2011-06-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=whip>Whipple, I.
